title: Natural multiplication and identity before the global monoid laws
statement: Let C be a category with pullbacks, J a Grothendieck topology, and {f_a:X_a→U} a covering family [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], in a containing universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Let A_a be sheaves of commutative monoids on C/X_a with isomorphisms phi_ab between their restrictions to C/(X_a×_U X_b). Let F be a set sheaf on C/U and let e_a:F|_{X_a}≅|A_a| be natural isomorphisms, satisfying e_b=phi_ab e_a on overlaps with the canonical comparison of the two composites to U, including a=b [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. There exist binary functions mul_V:F(V)×F(V)→F(V) and elements one_V∈F(V), natural in V, such that e_a carries mul to local multiplication and one to the local identity. No associativity, commutativity, unit laws, structure uniqueness, or structural map is asserted.

proof.text: Form P=F×F and the singleton sheaf T sectionwise. Mathlib Sheaf.tensorProd_isSheaf and tensorUnit_isSheaf implement the product and empty limits of lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise.

Define m_a(x,y)=e_a^{-1}(e_a(x)e_a(y)) and j_a(*)=e_a^{-1}(1). Naturality of e_a and its inverse, and multiplicativity and identity preservation of every A_a restriction, prove that these are natural transformations on each slice. Apply the injective phi_ab after e_a to the two overlap values. The equation for e and multiplicativity of phi_ab identify the two m_a; preservation of 1 gives the same identity for j_a.

Apply lem-trf-over-sheaf-map-gluing to (P,F,m_a) and (T,F,j_a). Define mul_V(x,y)=m_V(x,y) and one_V=j_V(*). Naturality of the glued transformations gives both restriction equations. The restriction formulas and e_a e_a^{-1}=id give their prescribed local multiplication and identity. The proof is complete in Lean from the one map-gluing theorem.

theorem monoidSheafLocalOperations
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasPullbacks C]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) {I : Type (max u v w)}
    (U : C) (X : I → C) (f : ∀ a, X a ⟶ U)
    (hcov : Sieve.ofArrows X f ∈ J U)
    (A : ∀ a, Sheaf (J.over (X a)) CommMonCat.{max u v w})
    (phi : ∀ a b,
      (J.overMapPullback CommMonCat (pullback.fst (f a) (f b))).obj (A a) ≅
        (J.overMapPullback CommMonCat (pullback.snd (f a) (f b))).obj (A b))
    (F : Sheaf (J.over U) (Type (max u v w)))
    (e : ∀ a, (Over.map (f a)).op ⋙ F.obj ≅ (A a).obj ⋙ forget CommMonCat)
    (he : ∀ (a b : I) (V : Over (pullback (f a) (f b)))
      (x : F.obj.obj (op ((Over.map (pullback.snd (f a) (f b)) ⋙
        Over.map (f b)).obj V))),
      (e b).hom.app _ x = (phi a b).hom.hom.app (op V)
        ((e a).hom.app _
          (F.obj.map (((Over.mapComp _ _).symm ≪≫
          Over.mapCongr _ _ (pullback.condition (f := f a) (g := f b)) ≪≫
          Over.mapComp _ _).hom.app V).op x))) :
    ∃ (mul : ∀ V : (Over U)ᵒᵖ, F.obj.obj V → F.obj.obj V → F.obj.obj V)
      (one : ∀ V : (Over U)ᵒᵖ, F.obj.obj V),
      ((∀ (V W : (Over U)ᵒᵖ) (k : V ⟶ W) (x y : F.obj.obj V),
          F.obj.map k (mul V x y) = mul W (F.obj.map k x) (F.obj.map k y)) ∧
        (∀ (V W : (Over U)ᵒᵖ) (k : V ⟶ W), F.obj.map k (one V) = one W)) ∧
      ((∀ (a : I) (V : (Over (X a))ᵒᵖ)
          (x y : F.obj.obj ((Over.map (f a)).op.obj V)),
          (e a).hom.app V (mul _ x y) = (e a).hom.app V x * (e a).hom.app V y) ∧
        (∀ (a : I) (V : (Over (X a))ᵒᵖ), (e a).hom.app V (one _) = 1))
